exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: A strong plan comparison names its variables and reads its graph — here is how one student compared gym memberships.

traits.sample: Months is my independent variable and total cost depends on it: c = 25m + 20 for the gym with a $20 sign-up fee.
traits.why: The relationship is stated with both variables defined.

traits.trait: Interprets the y-intercept in real life
traits.sample: The point (0, 20) means before any months pass, you already owe the $20 sign-up fee.
traits.why: It translates a graph point into money and time.

traits.sample: The $30-per-month gym with no fee is proportional — it starts at (0, 0) and doubles when months double; the fee plan does not.
traits.why: The test for proportionality is applied, not just named.

traits.sample: The lines cross at 4 months, so I recommend the fee plan only for people staying longer than 4 months.
traits.why: The recommendation depends on where the graphs intersect.
